questions.questionText: According to Carnot's theorem, which statement is true about heat engines operating between two temperatures?
options: A reversible engine can never be more efficient than an irreversible engine operating between the same temperatures.
A reversible engine can never be less efficient than an irreversible engine operating between the same temperatures.
No heat engine operating between two given temperatures can be more efficient than a reversible engine operating between the same temperatures.
All heat engines operating between two temperatures have the same efficiency.
questions.correctAnswer: No heat engine operating between two given temperatures can be more efficient than a reversible engine operating between the same temperatures.
questions.explanation: Carnot’s theorem states that a reversible engine sets the upper bound on efficiency for any engine between the same two reservoirs.

questions.questionText: The thermal efficiency of a heat engine is defined as the ratio of which two quantities?
options: Net work output to the heat rejected to the cold reservoir
Net work output to the heat absorbed from the hot reservoir
Heat rejected to the cold reservoir to the heat absorbed from the hot reservoir
Heat absorbed from the hot reservoir to the net work output
questions.correctAnswer: Net work output to the heat absorbed from the hot reservoir
questions.explanation: Efficiency η = W/Q_H, the useful work divided by the heat input.

questions.questionText: During the reversible isothermal expansion (process 1→2) of an ideal gas, what happens to its internal energy?
options: It increases proportionally to the volume change.
It decreases proportionally to the volume change.
It oscillates as the gas expands.
questions.explanation: For an ideal gas at constant temperature, ΔU = nC_VΔT = 0.

questions.questionText: Which relationship correctly links the volume ratios in the adiabatic processes of the Carnot cycle?
questions.explanation: From the adiabatic equations T_H V2^(γ−1)=T_C V3^(γ−1) and T_H V1^(γ−1)=T_C V4^(γ−1).

questions.questionText: What is the expression for the Carnot efficiency of a heat engine operating between temperatures T_H and T_C?
questions.explanation: Carnot efficiency depends only on the reservoir temperatures: η_Carnot = 1 − T_C/T_H.

questions.questionText: For a steam turbine operating between T_H = 800 K and T_C = 300 K, what is the maximum theoretical efficiency?
During the reversible adiabatic expansion (process 2→3) of the Carnot cycle, what happens to the working fluid’s temperature?
options: It increases from T_C to T_H
It decreases from T_H to T_C
It oscillates between T_H and T_C
questions.correctAnswer: It decreases from T_H to T_C
questions.explanation: Adiabatic expansion uses internal energy to do work, causing the temperature to drop.

questions.questionText: Which statement correctly describes the Clausius inequality for irreversible cycles?
questions.explanation: For irreversible cycles the cyclic integral of dQ/T is negative, indicating entropy generation.

questions.questionText: Which Carnot cycle process rejects heat Q_C to the cold reservoir?
questions.explanation: During isothermal compression at T_C, the gas rejects heat to the cold sink.
